main.note: Block 1: 3 rounds. Do Exercise A, then Exercise B straight away with no rest, then rest 60 s. Repeat. Antagonist superset. 3 s lowering on both.
Block 2: 3 rounds. Do Exercise A, then Exercise B straight away with no rest, then rest 45 s. Repeat. Antagonist superset.
Block 3: 2 rounds. Do Exercise A, then Exercise B straight away with no rest, then rest 45 s. Repeat. Antagonist superset.
Block 4: 2 rounds. Do Exercise A, then Exercise B straight away with no rest, then rest 30 s. Repeat. Forearm flexor-extensor superset.
Block 5: 3 rounds. Do Exercise A, then Exercise B straight away with no rest, then rest 45 s. Repeat. Biceps-brachialis superset.
Block 6: 3 rounds. Do Exercise A, then Exercise B straight away with no rest, then rest 30 s. Repeat.

My Fitness Profile and Goals
Item Detail

Body fat 20.3%

Primary goal Muscle hypertrophy and strength (especially biceps), with body recomposition: build lean mass
while reducing belly fat; about +3 kg lean-led body weight over roughly 10-14 weeks

Part 1: Training Overview
Eight-week programme summary
The programme builds muscle with limited dumbbell weight (max 5 kg per hand) by raising difficulty through tempo,
unilateral work, pauses, supersets, mechanical drop sets and tri-sets. Every week uses a different exercise selection for
each muscle group, and every training day includes a targeted warm-up, a main workout, muscle-specific stretching and
breathing practice.
Weekly training split (same pattern all 8 weeks, different exercises each
week)
Day Focus Muscle groups

Upper Abs

Abs
Wednesday Shoulders and Arms + Obliques (+ 15-20 min easy Front/side/rear delts, biceps, brachialis, triceps, obliques
cardio)
Thursday Hamstrings, Glutes, Calves + Deep Core Hamstrings, glutes, calves, lower back, deep core
Friday Back, Chest Support, Biceps, Forearms + Deep Lats, rhomboids, traps, rear delts, chest, biceps, forearms, deep
Core (+ 15-20 min easy cardio) core
Saturday Arms, Legs, Press Variations + Step-Board Cardio Biceps, triceps, quads, shoulders, core, cardio finisher
Sunday Active Recovery: cardio, full-body yoga, breathing Mobility, circulation, recovery
Intensity progression
Weeks Phase Intensity What changes
Weeks Phase 1: Foundation Medium Straight sets; 3-4 sets of 10-15 reps; 60-75 s rest; 3 RIR. Week 2 adds a set on
1-2 primary lifts and swaps every exercise pattern.
Weeks Phase 2: Build Medium-to-High Antagonist and compound supersets; 3-4 s eccentrics; 45 s rest inside rounds,
3-4 60 s after the pair; 2-3 RIR.
Weeks Phase 3: Overload High Supersets plus mechanical drop sets; 2 s pause reps; 4-5 s negatives; 30-45 s
5-6 rest; 1-2 RIR.
Weeks Phase 4: Peak Advanced Tri-sets, tempo work, controlled eccentrics, finishing exercises. Week 8 trims
7-8 volume (fewer rounds) so it is hard but not an overtraining week.
Recovery strategy
- Every muscle group is trained at most twice per week, with at least 48 hours (usually 3-4 days) between hard sessions
for the same group.

- Chest and back are paired on Monday and Friday (4 days apart). Quadriceps work (Tuesday) is separated from
hamstring/glute work (Thursday) by a full day.
- Saturday uses lighter, higher-rep leg and arm work and a short cardio finisher so Sunday recovery can restore you for
Monday.
- Sunday is a true recovery day: easy cardio, full-body yoga and breathing. It is never a second high-intensity session.
- Cardio stays low-impact: 3 min step-board warm-up, a Saturday finisher, two short fat-loss cardio sessions (Wednesday
and Friday, 15-20 min easy pace) and Sunday cardio, so it supports fat loss without competing with muscle recovery.
- Sleep 7-9 hours, hydrate, and follow the nutrition guidance. If recovery signs (see Nutrition and Recovery) appear, drop
one set from each exercise for a few days.

Progressive Overload and Intensity Management
Topic Guidance
Increase repetitions When you reach the top of the rep range on all sets with good form and 2-3 RIR, add 1-2 reps per set
next session. Do not increase sets at the same time.
Increase sets Only in Weeks 1-2 on primary lifts (3 to 4 sets). Later weeks use supersets and tri-sets instead of
adding more sets, and Week 8 trims sets.
Increase time under From Week 3 use 3-5 s lowering phases, from Week 5 add 2 s pauses, from Week 7 use 4-1-1 style
tension tempos. Do this before adding any reps.
Progress exercise difficulty With only 3 kg and 5 kg pairs, progress by making the movement harder: bilateral to unilateral
(Bulgarian split squat), flat to feet-elevated push-ups, two-hand to single-arm presses.
Reduce rest Rest drops from 60-75 s (Phase 1) to 45 s (Phase 2), 30-45 s (Phase 3) and short rests inside tri-sets
(Phase 4). Reduce rest only when reps are stable.
Do not change everything In any week change one or two variables only (for example tempo and rest), not reps, sets, tempo
at once and rest together.
Reps in reserve (RIR) Most working sets finish with 1-3 RIR. Go close to failure (0-1 RIR) only on the last set of isolation
exercises (raises, curls, extensions) and on bodyweight finishers, never on loaded single-leg
exercises or when form breaks.
Managing fatigue Keep 1-3 RIR on compound lifts, protect sleep, and if two sessions in a row drop below your reps,
remove one set from each exercise for 3-4 days. Week 8 is intentionally controlled.
Dumbbell weights Only 3 kg and 5 kg pairs are used. Raises, flies, kickbacks, extensions and rotations use 3 kg;
presses, rows, lunges, squats and curls use 5 kg. Holding one 5 kg dumbbell with both hands counts
as the load for goblet-style moves.
Muscle Gain, Nutrition and Recovery
Topic Guidance
Realistic expectations Goal: build muscle while reducing belly fat. Over 8 weeks expect roughly 1-1.5 kg of new lean mass
(body recomposition) and 0.5-1.5 kg of fat loss, so scale weight may rise only 0 to +1.5 kg while the waist shrinks and
arms, shoulders and legs improve. Gaining 3 kg of pure muscle in 8 weeks is not realistic; about +3
kg total is a 10-14 week outcome. Fat cannot be removed from the stomach alone: belly fat falls as
overall body fat falls, so waist measurement and photos matter more than the scale.
Calories Estimated maintenance is roughly 2,450-2,600 kcal per day (varies with job activity). For
recomposition eat at maintenance to a small surplus of 100-150 kcal, so about 2,550-2,700 kcal per
day. If weight rises faster than 0.2 kg per week or the waist grows, reduce by 100-150 kcal; if energy
and reps drop, add 100 kcal. Avoid a large surplus and avoid crash dieting.
Protein 1.8-2.0 g per kg body weight, about 125-140 g per day, split across 4-5 meals (25-35 g each).
Carbohydrate About 4.7-5.3 g per kg, about 330-370 g per day, from rice, oats, potatoes, fruit, bread and legumes.
Put a carbohydrate-rich meal within 2-3 hours before and after training.
Healthy fats About 1.0 g per kg, about 65-75 g per day, from nuts, olive oil, eggs, fish and avocado.
Hydration About 35-40 ml per kg per day (2.5-3 L), plus 500 ml extra on training days or hot days. Pale-yellow
urine is a good guide.
Sleep and recovery 7-9 hours per night. Keep a regular schedule; avoid screens for 30 minutes before bed.
Rest between sessions At least 48 hours between hard sessions for the same muscle group (built into the split).
Signs of inadequate Resting heart rate 5-8 bpm above normal for several mornings, persistent soreness beyond 72 hours,
recovery falling reps for two sessions, poor sleep, low mood or irritability, joint pain. Response: remove one set
per exercise for 3-4 days and add 100-150 kcal.
Progress monitoring Measure waist at the navel every week and take photos every 2 weeks; weigh yourself on the same
morning each week under the same conditions; record the body-composition device figures weekly
(treat as trends, they vary with hydration); take waist, chest and arm measurements every 2 weeks;
log every workout.
Supplements No steroids or unverified muscle-building products. Food comes first; creatine monohydrate (3-5 g
per day) and whey protein are the only commonly evidence-backed options and are optional. Check
with a doctor if you have any medical condition.
Medical note This programme is general fitness guidance, not medical advice. At age 41, if you have any heart,
blood pressure, joint or other health concerns, check with a doctor before starting.
